title: Ordering rational numbers
competency: Write rational numbers in ascending or descending order.

keywords.def: From the smallest to the largest.
From the largest to the smallest.

en.text: To order rational numbers, put them in the same form first: all with one common denominator, or all as decimals. Then line them up from smallest to largest (ascending) or largest to smallest (descending).

am.text: ሬሽናል ቁጥሮችን ለመደርደር መጀመሪያ በአንድ ዓይነት መልክ አስቀምጣቸው፤ በጋራ ተካፋይ ወይም በአስርዮሽ። ከዚያ ከትንሽ ወደ ትልቅ ወይም ከትልቅ ወደ ትንሽ ደርድራቸው።

screens.title: Samuel's plants
screens.text: Differences from the average growth: Rahel 3 1/4 cm, Kassa −2.2 cm, Alemitu 1.7 cm, Munir −1 7/10 cm.
screens.after:
Change all to decimals: Rahel 3 1/4 = 3.25, Kassa −2.2, Alemitu 1.7, Munir −1 7/10 = −1.7.
The biggest number is 3.25.
So Rahel's plant grew the most.
Kassa and Munir have negative numbers: they grew less than average.

screens.title: Ordering rational numbers
paras: Ordering means writing numbers in ascending or descending order.
It is like ordering distances in miles and kilometres: use one unit first.
For fractions, use one common denominator. Or change them to decimals.

screens.title: Samuel's plants on the number line

points.info: Kassa: 2.2 cm below the average. Furthest left, so the lowest.
Rahel: 3 1/4 = 3.25 cm. Furthest right, so the highest.

screens.ask: Tap the points from left to right. Left is smaller, so this is ascending order.

screens.title: Key words
defs: From the smallest to the largest.
From the largest to the smallest.

screens.title: Order the integers in ascending order (smallest first)
screens.why:
Negatives come first: −45 and −25.
−45 has the bigger size, so it is further left: −45 < −25.
Then the positives by size: 18 < 28 < 30.
Order: −45, −25, 18, 28, 30.
screens.clue: Negatives first; the bigger negative size is smaller.

steps: The denominators are 5, 9, 3, 6 and 18. Their LCM is 90.

screens.title: Order the decimals in ascending order (smallest first)
Order the integers in descending order (largest first)
screens.why:
Positives first, largest first: 45 > 32.
Then the negatives.
−15 has the smaller size, so it is closer to 0 and bigger: −15 > −23.
Order: 45, 32, −15, −23.

screens.title: Samuel's plants: order the differences from lowest to highest
screens.why:
Change to decimals: −1 7/10 = −1.7 and 3 1/4 = 3.25.
Negatives first: −2.2 has the bigger size, so −2.2 < −1.7.
Then positives: 1.7 < 3.25.
Order: −2.2, −1 7/10, 1.7, 3 1/4.

screens.title: Order the rational numbers in ascending order (smallest first)
screens.clue: Change every number to a decimal. 5/7 is a little more than 0.7.

items.title: Order the decimals in ascending order (smallest first)
items.why:
The only negative, −12.51, comes first.
Then compare integer parts: 5 < 6 < 8 < 12.
Order: −12.51, 5.24, 6.75, 8.13, 12.42.

items.text: Compare the plants: whose plant grew the most? (Rahel 3 1/4, Kassa −2.2, Alemitu 1.7, Munir −1 7/10)
items.why:
Change to decimals: 3.25, −2.2, 1.7 and −1.7.
The largest number is 3.25.
That is Rahel's.
So Rahel's plant grew the most.

items.title: Samuel's plants: order the differences from lowest to highest

test.title: Order the numbers in ascending order (smallest first)
test.why:
Change to decimals: −1/2 = −0.5, 1/3 ≈ 0.33, 3/4 = 0.75.
The negative comes first: −0.5.
Then 0.33 < 0.5 < 0.75.
Order: −1/2, 1/3, 0.5, 3/4.

test.title: Order the numbers in descending order (largest first)
test.why:
Change to decimals: 2 1/4 = 2.25.
Positives: 2.5 > 2.25.
Negatives: −1 is closer to 0 than −1.5, so −1 > −1.5.
Order: 2.5, 2 1/4, −1, −1.5.

test.text: Compare fractions and decimals: which is the smallest: 3/4, 0.7, 5/8?
test.why:
Change to decimals: 3/4 = 0.75 and 5/8 = 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625.
Compare 0.75, 0.70 and 0.625.
Tenths: 7, 7 and 6.
The smallest is 0.625 = 5/8.

test.text: Ascending order: which list goes from smallest to largest?
test.why:
Change to decimals: 3/4 = 0.75.
Negatives first: −2 < −1.5 (−2 is further left).
Then positives: 0.5 < 0.75.
So −2, −1.5, 0.5, 3/4 is ascending. (−1.5, −2, … puts −1.5 first, but −2 is smaller.)
